text.p: Albania's state secretary for sports, Marjeta Pronjari, expressed regret on Thursday about her country's suspension by world soccer's governing body FIFA and vowed to step up efforts to get Albania reinstated.
"This is a fatal situation. We will try to find a solution which is in the interest of the country," said Pronjari, a former high jumper.

FIFA suspended Albania indefinitely after Pronjari's ministry ordered the suspension of the Albanian Football Association's (AFA) general secretary Edvard Dervishi and dissolved the executive committee.
Pronjari added had simply respected her country's law in sacking Dervishi and shrugged off all charges of intervention.

The ban puts Albania's World Cup group nine qualifying match against Northern Ireland on December 14 in jeopardy and Northern Ireland have asked FIFA to tell them by Tuesday if the match in Belfast would go ahead as planned.
Pronjari reiterated that Dervishi was suspended for having continuously postponed new executive committee elections, therefore breaking Albania's civil law.
But FIFA fully backed AFA, saying it did not recognise these decisions and would continue considering Dervishi and the dissolved executive as their only official contacts in Albania.
Pronjari said she had contacted the FIFA and the president of AFA, Edmond Spaho, on Thursday to discuss the matter.
